rationale: Roberts is likely to keep the opinion narrow and administrable: insurance proceeds are corporate assets at death under § 2031/Reg. § 20.2031-2(f), and a mandatory redemption is not a debt-like liability that nets out value. A Kagan-led dissent (possibly joined by Sotomayor and Gorsuch) is the most probable separate writing, emphasizing Cartwright’s fully informed buyer and the claimed double-counting of earmarked proceeds.
